text.p: Swedish steelmaker SSAB is expected to post a profit after financial items of 1.66 billion crowns for the first nine months of the year, a Reuter poll of 12 analysts' forecasts showed on Monday.
The forecasts ranged between 1.51 billion crowns and 1.79 billion. SSAB posted earnings of 1.42 billion crowns in the corresponding period last year.
The analysts forecast a profit of 2.13 billion crowns for the full year, slightly down on the 2.15 reported for 1995.
Profits for 1997 were seen rising to 2.42 billion crowns, rising to 3.02 billion in 1998.
The analysts in the survey were not in agreement on when steel prices would take an upturn from the current low levels.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Handelsbanken, Swedbank, Enskilda, Foreningsbanken, Matteus, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Fiba Nordic, Aros, Carnegie, Alfred Berg, Penser FK, James Capel.
SSAB's nine-month report is due for release on October 31. (Skr million) Average Range Analysts
